cards.lof: Nick Ilias started Left of Field in his brother’s old bedroom in 2022, working from surf and skate silhouettes rather than golf ones — “our mission isn’t to create products that scream ‘golf’.” Every collection takes its name from a stretch of Australian coast: Elements for Barnbougle in Tasmania, SOUTH for the Mornington Peninsula, RNP for Royal National Park below Sydney. The sustainability page commits to recycled-PET yarn, which almost nobody this size does.
cards.walker: Jack Fardell runs Walker out of the Gold Coast, a professional skateboarder whose father named him after Jack Nicklaus — “I didn’t really have a choice but to play golf.” The collaborations come constantly: Evan Mock’s Wahine, Coopers the brewery, Shortees the floodlit Sydney par-three. Riding for adidas Skateboarding since 2015 is how a small label ended up with an adidas Golf capsule in 2024, built around a co-designed MC-Z Traxion shoe.
cards.penta: Penta is three friends who met working at a creative print magazine and a youth-culture agency, and who have never put their names on the site. The Etiquette Pants and the PXB line with Barnaby’s read like a magazine art department made golf clothes. Asked where they play, they were specific: “anywhere on the Northern Beaches… but Warringah Golf Club is our local.” The last drop was December 2025, so the range is stocked but static.
cards.midiron: Midiron has made nine products in eight months and named nobody behind them. Most of it is shot at night under a hard flash on a floodlit par-three, and every second product page signs off “Golf Apparel Research approved” — Golf Apparel Research being their own house name. The best thing they have made is a reworked vintage Titleist cap, sold as three one-offs, with an unsigned story about a grandad’s hand-me-down underneath it.
cards.birds: Birds of Condor began with Frankie Kimpton sneaking out of his booking-agent job at Mushroom Records to hit balls at Albert Park in black jeans and a Guns N’ Roses shirt — “I think it was 20 bucks for a bucket of balls and a beer.” The first drop was ten hats. Several hundred products and a Culture Kings stockist list later, the Byron Bay flagship holds a restored 1980s buggy from Sanctuary Cove.
cards.okka: One person screen-prints everything Okka sells, in Perth, and keeps it that way on purpose. The answer to wholesale, posted on their own site, is “no bueno amigo. not something i do. i’m extremely protective of the relationship i have with frens of OKKA.” Every piece is shot the same way on the same backdrop, like a lookbook made by someone who only owns one light.
cards.grayhaast: Gray is the founder’s surname and Haast is for the Haast’s eagle, the largest eagle known to have existed, which makes the name a joke about the score every golfer chases and never makes. The clothing is the most conventionally handsome of the Australian brands, and the Peninsula long-sleeve polo and the Performance Shell are the two to start with. Noosa Golf Co stocks them, and new product lands regularly.
cards.found: Lance Peach and Ellen Keillar have run Found since 2022, and thirty-five of their fifty-eight products are art rather than apparel — paintings, sculpture, a bench listed at nearly six thousand dollars. The clothing that does exist is made where possible with boutique ateliers in Cape Town, with the ex-AFL player Dale Thomas as creative partner. They also sell golf tees in a reusable cigarette box, which tells you the register.
cards.mackem: Mackem makes wool-blend headcovers and waxed-canvas pouches, all sewn in-house in the Perth hills, with a real shop on Haynes Street you can walk into. The bespoke work has turned football shirts, wedding suits and boardshorts into covers, and one set came from a family tartan embroidered with the initials of a customer’s late father. Adam is blunt about scaling: “we’re not Amazon Prime and never want to be.”
cards.bigdog: Mark Calder started Big Dog on a dining table in a Brunswick apartment in 2019, having noticed that The Big Dog® was common shorthand for the driver and that nobody had trademarked it. The leather covers now sit in the pro shops at Royal Melbourne, Barnbougle, Royal Adelaide, Peninsula Kingswood and Cape Wickham, plus Tara Iti and Te Arai Links across the Tasman. If you are building an Australian trip, this is the souvenir.
cards.#11: Random Golf Club takes fourteen players through Kingston Heath, Victoria, Peninsula Kingswood North, both Nationals and St Andrews Beach, opening at Royal Park, the Melbourne public course where the first meetup happened. Al and Erik Anders Lang drive the vans themselves, promising “a smaller group and no fixed leash.” Golf, lodging, transport and breakfast are in; airfare and caddies are not. It finishes with 36 holes of matchplay for the Random Cup.
cards.#12: Air Adventure Australia has flown out of regional Victoria since 1977, and the Big 5 puts you in a Pilatus PC-12 that lands at the course — “as little as 90 minutes from take-off to tee-off.” That is the clean answer to King Island, where no passenger ferry crosses Bass Strait. Five days covers Barnbougle Dunes, Lost Farm, Seven Mile Beach, Cape Wickham and Ocean Dunes, with a A$285 surcharge for international players.

kickers.1: Australia’s independent golf scene got good fast, and in a specific way: surf and skate silhouettes, coastal names, and no interest in looking like a pro shop. All eight ship internationally, and most price in Australian dollars.
kickers.2: Two small workshops sew the other half of the Australian scene by hand, and the work has ended up in the best pro shops in the country — Big Dog’s covers sit at Royal Melbourne, Barnbougle and Cape Wickham. If you are going, start here rather than at the logoed cap.
kickers.3: Random Golf Club runs an Australia trip; no other golf-media or apparel brand in the world does. Across roughly twenty operators, not one described a private Sandbelt tee time as guaranteed — access is sold as capability, never as contract.
kickers.4: The other ten are best compared on price and round count rather than on marketing. Read the AUSGOLF line carefully: that A$2,525 is a rate for Golf Australia members, and overseas surcharges apply without being quantified. Premier’s low headline buys four rounds across ten days.
